prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1272; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a side impact at a controlled intersection. The claimant, who is represented by counsel, was a passenger in the other vehicle and has reported a head injury.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it and the coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the responding officer, who confirms the claimant was in the vehicle when it was attended. No independent witness, photograph, or other report of the collision has been located so far.

Entry 4: Inspected the insured vehicle. The damage to the driver side door and rear quarter panel matches the described angle and force of a side impact.

Entry 5: Inspected the claimant's vehicle. Found no earlier damage in the affected areas, and the repair estimate lines up with the impact described in the first report.

Entry 6: Claimant's counsel sent a letter outlining a concussion diagnosis with ongoing headaches. The injury is consistent with the kind and force of the crash.

Entry 7: Obtained medical records covering the first treatment visits. Treatment followed a usual course, and the claimant reported steady improvement over the following weeks.

Entry 8: Checked prior claim and medical history. No earlier injury to the same body area is on record.

Entry 9: Took a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account of how the collision happened matches what was told in every earlier conversation.

Entry 10: Reviewed the latest treatment notes. Symptoms have tapered off, and the treating provider expects a full recovery without further specialist care.

Entry 11: Reviewed the file with the supervisor. Liability and injury evaluation are documented, and the claim is ready for settlement discussions with counsel.
